evidence.text: He does ask Shepard if the Commander keeps some fish in the Captain's Cabin, however. Soon after being integrated into the Normandy team, Liara contacts Javik, talking with him about the Collectors and Shepard's role in destroying them. Javik is initially unhappy at more of his race being wiped out but realizes that they were indoctrinated. He tells Liara that he is grateful that Shepard killed them, calling it an act of mercy. Later, Liara contacts him again on the comm, trying to pry more information out of him about the Crucible. Javik is irritated at her persistence and snaps at her to let him recover. He tells Shepard that he wishes that the asari had never learned to talk. After the krogan female's retrieval from Sur'Kesh as part of the scheme to forge a turian\-krogan alliance for the war, Javik has an intercom conversation with Liara, asking her why she is so interested in his species. She explains her fascination with Protheans, believing his species to be enlightened. She wonders what it would be like to wake up to a new galaxy. Javik states his belief that this cycle cares too much about what other species think. He asks what saving Eve accomplishes in uniting the krogan, turians and salarians. Liara reminds him that they can't defeat the Reapers alone, though Javik states that they must demand the other races' help, not give in to their selfish requests. Liara states that it's not that simple. Javik growls that they should destroy them if they refuse. He apologizes for the last comment, admitting that some of Grunt's aggression has rubbed off on him. After conversing with Liara, Javik asks Shepard why Cerberus would oppose what they're doing. He states that they will bleed like everyone else when the Reapers are not stopped. Javik comments on Lieutenant Victus' disastrous mission after Shepard's meet\-up with the stranded turians on Tuchanka. If Victus had been under his command, he would've marooned him in the desert, buried him up to his neck in sand and let the wildlife feast on his eyes. And if Victus survived all that, Javik would have rewarded him by shooting him in the head. He declares that good soldiers are precious resources and the stupidity of one should not be allowed to jeopardize the lives of the others. After the Tuchanka bomb's defusal, Javik converses with Garrus over the comm, complimenting that his race would've made a fine addition to the Prothean Empire due to their cunning; they dispute over whether "slave race" or "subservient race" are different. However, he criticizes the turians for failing to detonate the bomb or use it as leverage against the krogan. Garrus states that they are just trying to keep the peace. Javik retorts that nothing changes because of it. Garrus adds that on the plus side, they all get to live another day. When the investigation into rachni in the Attican Traverse has concluded and if Javik was not present during the mission, he shares how the Protheans used the rachni as weapons. The Prothean scientists were more interested in rachni biology than in their ability to sing thoughts to each other. The Protheans bred the rachni to be obedient and battle\-ready, using selective breeding to encourage the development of ever more cunning and aggressive Rachni Queens, and unleashed them on their enemies till the rachni turned on their masters. Javik also says that the rachni proved that the universe favors the strong, as the rachni managed to survive the extermination attempts on them for two cycles. After the genophage has been dealt with, Javik tells Shepard of a deal he would have offered the salarian dalatrass, had he been in their place. He would have sabotaged the cure and obtained both salarian and krogan help. If the Commander did sabotage the cure, Javik is able to sense it and approves of their actions. During one of the after mission lulls, after saving Grissom Academy students from the clutches of Cerberus, Javik is found in Jack's former quarters, exploring the ship. If the psychotic biotic was encountered, Javik says there are traces of her lingering anger and pain in the room. He can sense whether Shepard helped fulfill her goal of taking revenge against Cerberus, hoping the Commander does the same for him, or that he'll have better fortune under Shepard's command than Jack did. If Jack was never encountered, Javik instead comments on the human\-turian effort that went into the Normandy's design. He asks if the turians were subservient, and Shepard says it was a joint effort. Javik shares the Prothean mindset of distrust, saying they would never have allowed that. He cautions that perhaps the turians may betray them later, which Shepard takes under advisement.

evidence.text:
Javik was the only known survivor of the ancient Prothean race, revived in 2186 after more than 50,000 years in stasis and driven by vengeance against the Reapers for his people's extinction. He was written mainly by John Dombrow and added through the From Ashes DLC, fully integrated into the Legendary Edition.

In Prothean society, "Avatars" each embodied a single virtue; Javik's was Vengeance. Born mid-war on a galaxy already losing to the Reapers, he was to lead roughly one million warriors who would outlast the invasion in stasis in an underground bunker on Eden Prime, then reclaim the galaxy. Indoctrinated traitors betrayed the bunker to the Reapers, and the Collectors slaughtered the sleeping Protheans. The supervising VI Victory initiated a neutron purge that damaged the bunker's sensors, making mass reactivation impossible; power was triaged so that only Javik would wake.

Commander Shepard and Liara T'Soni uncovered and opened his pod on Eden Prime while investigating Cerberus. Javik attacked them on waking, then agreed to join the fight to destroy the Reapers. Through touch he could read biological memories and instantly learned human language. He held imperialist, social-Darwinist views: he preached the "Cosmic Imperative," dismissed mercy, morality, and friendship as weakness, believed allies were merely resources, and thought the modern "primitive" races should be forced to help rather than asked. He refused to use names, referring to people by species or job. He took Grunt's former quarters aboard the Normandy and clashed repeatedly with the crew, especially EDI, whose capacity for choice he found troubling, and Liara, whose persistent questions and asari heritage he needled. He recounted Prothean history with the rachni (bred as weapons), the zha and synthetic zha'til, the densorin, and the asari, whom the Protheans secretly "guided" as this cycle's best hope, a claim that nearly provoked Liara to violence over events on Thessia.

If persuaded to use his Prothean Echo Shard, Javik relived hunting down and killing his own indoctrinated crew, concluding that war is atrocity committed for survival. Asked what he would do after the war, he might choose to return to the Cronian Nebula to take his own life and rejoin his comrades, or, if reconciled with Liara, co-author a book with her titled "Journeys with the Prothean," or live among the hanar on Kahje. In the Citadel DLC he starred alongside Shepard in "Blasto 7: Blasto Goes to War." If Shepard lacked sufficient forces, Javik could be killed by Harbinger in the final push; if he survived, he honored Shepard at the Memorial Wall. "Javik" derives from the Hindi word for "biological" or "organic."

evidence.text:
Vendetta was a Prothean Virtual Intelligence residing within a Prothean beacon in the Temple of Athame on Thessia. It was modeled after Pashek Vran, the overseer of the Protheans' Crucible project, and held valuable information about the Crucible's construction and implementation. During the Reaper assault on Thessia in 2186, Commander Shepard activated Vendetta. After verifying it was in a post-Prothean cycle and detecting Reapers, it attempted to shut down, declaring the cycle had reached its "extinction terminus," but Shepard urged it to wait.

Vendetta explained that the Crucible was not of Prothean design, and that the Protheans' attempt to use it had been sabotaged by an indoctrinated splinter group who argued the Reapers should be controlled rather than destroyed, much like Cerberus. It said the Protheans had found that similar patterns of evolution and dissolution recurred in every galactic cycle, too similar to be coincidence, and inferred the Reapers were merely "servants" of that pattern, not its creators, its intention being galactic annihilation. If Javik was present, Vendetta identified him as Prothean and revealed it had known of his mission. It agreed to help with the Catalyst once the Crucible was complete, then detected the indoctrinated Kai Leng and entered a fail-safe mode; Kai Leng, aided by an A-61 Mantis Gunship, defeated Shepard, took the VI, and delivered it to the Illusive Man.

At Cronos Station, Shepard learned from Vendetta that the Catalyst was the Citadel itself, which enhanced dark energy emissions and coordinated the mass relay network to extend the Crucible's range. Vendetta had been programmed to withhold this so the Reapers would not learn of it before the Crucible was finished, but the Illusive Man broke its security and informed the Reapers, who seized the Citadel and moved it into orbit of Earth. After Kai Leng's death, Vendetta reported the Reapers were preparing to complete the harvest of humanity and recommended preserving information for the next cycle. Like the other Prothean VIs Vigil and Victory, its name began with the letter V.

evidence.text:
Feron was a drell information trafficker who described himself as "an information trader. Not a slaver." In Mass Effect: Redemption, set after the destruction of the Normandy SR-1, Liara T'Soni hired him to help find Commander Shepard; he reported that Shepard was neither dead nor alive. Ambushed by Blue Suns sent by the Shadow Broker to delay Liara, the pair were saved by an unknown sniper, then encountered Cerberus agents, including Miranda Lawson, and were brought to the Illusive Man, who revealed the Shadow Broker was working with the Collectors. Feron admitted he had been ordered to lead Liara away from Shepard but chose to help her instead.

Feron took Liara to Afterlife on Omega, where Aria T'Loak resided, and learned where the Blue Suns would bring Shepard's body. He spotted the Broker's enforcer Tazzik but missed his ship with a turret, letting Tazzik flee Omega with the body. Feron revealed he had never stopped working for the Shadow Broker, which they could exploit to track Tazzik. The two infiltrated the Broker's base on Alingon, with Feron passing Liara off as his prisoner; he downloaded the Broker's dealings while Liara distracted a hologram of the Broker. Feron confessed Cerberus had recruited him and that he and the Illusive Man had planned for Feron to snatch the body. When a Collector exposed him as a traitor, Feron held off Tazzik so Liara could escape, and was captured.

In Mass Effect 2, Liara mentioned a "friend" lost during her search. During Lair of the Shadow Broker, Liara, Shepard, and Cerberus intel led to the Shadow Broker Base on Hagalaz, where Feron was found being tortured on a device that could not be removed without killing him. Liara and Shepard killed the Shadow Broker; Liara took over the role, and Feron chose to stay and assist her, mentally scarred and using his drell memory recall to survive the torture. In Mass Effect 3, if Shepard helped Liara take the Broker ship, Feron helped evacuate it during a Cerberus attack, became one of Liara's agents controlling Terminus operations (to Tazzik's dismay), and emailed Shepard offering information via Glyph. If Shepard did not help overthrow the Broker, Liara hired mercenaries to storm the lair and Feron did not survive.

evidence.text: As the Normandy's resident Prothean expert, Liara skills are brought to bear in an artifact retrieval mission on Eden Prime. Upon reaching the excavation site, Liara showcases her expertise depending on whether she already has a rapport with the squad. If she wasn't really close to the team, Liara launches into an explanation of Prothean architectural evolution. If she had significantly more interactions with the group, the other squadmate invariably asks if she has ever uncovered a dinosaur. Liara smartly delineates the differences between paleontology and archaeology before realizing she's being yanked around. Liara is surprised at learning they weren't retrieving just some Prothean artifact: what was unearthed, in fact, was a working stasis pod with a live Prothean inside. She helps Shepard in retrieving the command signals needed to safely open the pod while dealing with Cerberus forces in the area. When the dust has settled, she bears witness to the reawakening of the last Prothean in the galaxy: Javik. Liara is initially overjoyed to have a real living Prothean onboard the Normandy. However, following several conversations with him, she slowly grows disappointed. Having previously imagined Protheans as the "keepers of wisdom and enlightenment" of their era, Liara finds them to be cold and ruthless imperialistic warlords. In the aftermath of a mission when asked if she is working on anything Liara will explain that she's trying to decode some of the Crucibles designs, though theoretical particle physics were not her specialty. She laments how Javik is still being withdrawn, and how she wishes she could trade the last 100 years of her life to resurrect one Prothean scientist to help them. After the fall of Thessia, she can be found in Javik's cabin caught in a fierce argument with its occupant. Liara vehemently disbelieves the implication of Prothean involvement in asari history, and interprets Javik's blunt replies as gloating. Shepard can choose to defuse the situation, which results in a tentative peace between the two. Both sides slowly grow to respect and appreciate each other over time and, if Javik does not touch his memory shard, are thinking of writing a book together titled "Journeys with the Prothean". If Shepard didn't interrupt them, Liara decides he's not worth fighting and storms off Javik's quarters. Shepard can follow her to her cabin whichever way the argument ends and provide words of comfort.

evidence.text:
Priority: Mars was the first full mission of Mass Effect 3, acquired automatically after the Reaper assault on Earth in the prologue. Admiral Hackett ordered the Normandy to the Prothean archives on Mars, where the dig site had gone silent, to recover data that might help defeat the Reapers. Shepard landed with James Vega and found Cerberus troops executing Alliance researchers; this was the first appearance of Cerberus as an enemy faction in the trilogy, introducing Assault Troopers, Centurions and Guardians. Among the dead was a researcher named Reeves.

Inside the facility Shepard reunited with Dr. Liara T'Soni, who revealed she had discovered Prothean plans for a device ("the Crucible") capable of stopping the Reapers, and that Cerberus was there to seize them. Shepard sent Vega back to the shuttle to protect the team's exit and took Liara as squadmate. The two fought through the research complex, a sabotaged cafeteria where the air had been vented, corridors, a clean room, an autoturret gauntlet and a tram station, learning that Cerberus operatives had been implanted with Reaper technology. Shepard posed as a Cerberus team to lure a tram, then fought through a large battle at the archive station.

In the archive chamber the Illusive Man appeared by hologram. The Cerberus infiltrator Dr. Eva Coré was caught stealing the Prothean data, triggering a rooftop chase. Eva reached a shuttle, but Vega crashed his shuttle into hers. Her organic disguise was destroyed, revealing a mech infiltration unit, and on the Illusive Man's order she gravely injured Kaidan Alenko or Ashley Williams before Shepard shot her down. Shepard ordered the body brought aboard the Normandy, which left Mars orbit just as the Reapers arrived. The wounded crewmate was taken to the medical bay, and Shepard ordered Joker to set course for the Citadel. Hackett confirmed Anderson's order to seek Council aid and requested the Crucible plans for Alliance analysis. Eva's body would later be reactivated by EDI.
